chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Daqqaq, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Umar, from Zayd al-Qattat, from Aban ibn Taghlub, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'There is no servant who commits a sin and regrets it, except that Allah forgives him before he seeks forgiveness; and there is no servant upon whom Allah bestows a favor, so he recognizes that it is from Allah, except that Allah forgives him before he praises Him.'
ai.seo_question: How does sincere regret and recognition of blessings lead to divine forgiveness before explicit supplication?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi underscores the profound efficacy of internal sincerity (ikhlas) in Shia theology, suggesting that genuine remorse and recognition of divine grace are so potent that they secure forgiveness prior to the formal performance of istighfar or hamd. It reflects the concept of 'sabr jamil' and the mercy of Allah who looks at the heart's state before the tongue's utterance, a theme often cited by scholars like Al-Shaykh al-Mufid to emphasize the spiritual reality over ritual formality.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ali Bin Al Husayn Al Daqqaq, from Abdullah Bin Muhammad, from Abdullah Bin Muhammad, from Ahmad Bin Umar, from Zayd Al Qattab, from Aban Bin Taghlub who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘There is none from a servant who commits a sin and he regrets over it, except that Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Forgives it for him even before he seeks Forgiveness; and there is none from a servant upon whom Allah<sup>azwj</sup> has Favoured upon with a Bounty, so he recognises that it is from the Presence of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, except that Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Forgives (his sins) for him before he even Praises Him<sup>azwj</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 8. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from al-Husayn al-Daqqaq from ‘Abd Allah ibn Muhammad from Ahmad ibn ‘Umar from Zayd al-Qattat from Aban ibn Taghlib who has said the following:

“I heard abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) saying, ‘If a servant commits a sin and then regrets, Allah forgives him before he asks forgiveness. If a servant receives a favor from Allah and he learns that it is from Allah, He grants him forgiveness (protection) before he offers his thanks.’”
